name: Tier default by the tier's own metric
purpose: The default for each of the four tiers (fast, balanced, quality, best) is the arm that scores highest on that tier's own metric over public evaluations (metric-tier-fast, metric-tier-balanced, metric-tier-quality, metric-tier-best); the hub's own measured work per cost (metric-tier-passing-work-per-cost) overrides it only with the shared cases per arm that tier_metrics.csv names as the threshold.
record: Per tier: the arms' public evaluation rows (tier_public_scores.csv), the tier's weights (tier_metrics.csv), the score breakdown, and which arm the chooser picks and why.
disadvantages: A changed price, a new model or a leaderboard revision moves the ranking unseen until the rows are refreshed (45 days); the weights are the owner's judgment of what each tier is for, not a measured fact. Cascade rule added on 2026-11-10 after the rankings were seen, because the public ranking would have raised cost for an install with one provider: cheap evidence (public numbers) may select an arm whose list price (input plus output per million tokens at the base price row, the same at every effort) is at or below the held default's; an arm that costs more is returned as proposed and becomes the default only when the own-measurement stage confirms it on shared cases. Best is exempt because cost is not a factor there.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the registry and tier-selection tests pass] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read] > staged [sample=sample | real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the tier default is being challenged and the spend is approved]

name: Tier passing work per cost
purpose: The selector picks the arm with the most passing work per dollar, with every arm on the same cases.
record: Per tier: passing cases, tokens and the price on file for each arm.
disadvantages: A price that changed since its checked date moves the ranking unseen.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=hubofhubs/the_world/tests/test_tiers.py passes] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a single real case runs end to end and is hand-read] > measured [real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the held arm and the candidate are both measured on the shared cases and every price row has a current checked_on]

name: Model quality on hard maths
purpose: How well each current model does exact-answer AIME 2025 problems under one prompt, so the tier selector chooses on measured passing work per cost.
record: Cases passed over the 30 AIME 2025 I and II problems; tokens priced from tier_prices.csv or counted in calls on a subscription.
disadvantages: 30 problems and one run per model leave wide intervals; the problem text is fetched from a pinned mirror, not committed.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the scorer passes the reference answer of every case and fails the no-answer floor; no model, no cost] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a model answers one problem end to end and is hand-read] > sample [sample=sample:3 | real=yes | gate=competitive | when=the one passed] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | max-age-days=90 | when=the three passed and the spend is approved]
command: esoi run model_quality_aime --impl claude_haiku; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl claude_sonnet; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl claude_opus; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl gemini_2_5_flash_lite; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl gemini_2_5_flash; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl gpt_5_nano; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl gpt_5_mini; esoi run model_quality_aime --impl deepseek_flash

name: Vendor arms answer
purpose: Each vendor at its cheapest current model answers exact-answer maths word problems, as evidence for which vendor serves a tier (vendors are complementary and are not ranked as rivals).
record: Cases passed over a fixed sample of 50 GSM8K test problems, with tokens priced at the cheapest model of each vendor and the cost counted in the score.
disadvantages: Vendor arms are not ranked: 50 problems and one prompt leave wide intervals.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [sample=full | real=no | gate=all-pass | when=the scorer passes the reference answer of every case and fails the no-answer floor; no model, no cost] > one [sample=sample:1 | real=yes | gate=all-pass | when=a vendor key or subscription is available: one problem answers end to end and is hand-read] > sample [sample=sample:10 | real=yes | min-pass-rate=0.8 | when=the one passed] > whole [sample=full | real=yes | max-age-days=90 | when=the ten passed and the spend is approved; the vendors are evidence for the tier choice and are not ranked]
command: esoi run call_a_model --impl gemini; esoi run call_a_model --impl openai; esoi run call_a_model --impl deepseek; esoi run call_a_model --impl claude_cli

name: Fast tier default
purpose: The fast tier's default is the (provider, model, effort) arm that gives the most capability per unit of cost and time on structured and short tasks, among arms that clear an accuracy floor.
record: Public evaluations only until the hub has its own cases. Score = C^0.40 x K^0.30 x S^0.30, weights fixed in tier_metrics.csv before any ranking. C = 0.50 x AutomationBench-AA + 0.25 x AA-Omniscience accuracy + 0.25 x AA-Omniscience non-hallucination, each divided by the best eligible value. K = cheapest eligible cost per task divided by the arm's cost per task; S = fastest eligible time per task divided by the arm's. Floors: AutomationBench-AA at least 0.60 and Omniscience accuracy at least 0.50 of the best eligible value. A model with no number on a required measure is not eligible and nothing is imputed; rows older than 45 days are not used.
disadvantages: Cost and time per task are Artificial Analysis's cost and time of running its own index tasks, not of one short call; no public evaluation covers classification or extraction on current models (IFBench has no current rows), so AutomationBench-AA and the Omniscience pair stand in; one aggregator supplies every number, a second independent board (the Vals Index) is read as a cross-check only. Two validity rules were added on 2026-11-10 after the first ranking was seen, because that ranking would have raised cost for an install with one provider (fast would have become a mid model): (1) fit of evidence: every evaluation here is marked proxy in tier_metrics.csv, so the tier does not select from public numbers, the held default stays and the proxy ranking is returned for information; the hub's own measurements are the intended evidence, namely the cases (the threshold is the own_stage row of tier_metrics.csv) per arm of the tier's own prompts (classification, routing, extraction, retrieval queries) scored by their own metrics, the same cases for every arm compared; (2) effort must be real: an arm at an effort other than the vendor's documented default competes only when its caller applies the effort (none does today), so the cost assumed is the cost paid.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=hubofhubs/the_world/model_plumbing/tests/test_tier_public_metric.py passes] > public [real=no | gate=competitive | max-age-days=45 | when=every required public row of the arm is present and no older than 45 days, and the arm's list price (input plus output per million tokens) is no higher than the held default's; a dearer arm is only proposed] > own [real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the hub has run the shared cases that tier_metrics.csv names as the threshold for each arm compared and the spend is approved]

name: Balanced tier default
purpose: The balanced tier's default is the arm with the most capability on agentic coding, tool use and writing per unit of cost and time, among arms that reach 0.70 of the best eligible capability.
record: Score = C^0.55 x K^0.25 x S^0.20, weights fixed in tier_metrics.csv before any ranking. C = 0.20 x Terminal-Bench 4.0 + 0.20 x FrontierCode 2.0 + 0.25 x AutomationBench-AA + 0.20 x GDPval-AA (Elo read as the chance of beating the best arm) + 0.15 x AA-Omniscience non-hallucination, each divided by the best eligible value. K and S as for the fast tier. Floor: C at least 0.70. No imputation: a missing required number makes the arm ineligible; rows older than 45 days are not used.
disadvantages: Same cost and time caveat as the fast tier; GDPval-AA is missing for some models, which makes them ineligible here until it is published; coding scores come from one harness (Artificial Analysis's Stirrup) and vendor harnesses may rank differently. Cost per task is a proxy for the cost of the tier's typical call (long agentic tasks, not one call). Two validity rules were added on 2026-11-10 after the first ranking was seen, because that ranking would have raised cost for an install with one provider: the evaluations must fit the tier's use (marked direct in tier_metrics.csv; here they carry more than half of the weight, so the tier selects) and an arm at a non-default effort competes only when its caller applies the effort (none does today, so only each model's documented default effort competes).
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=hubofhubs/the_world/model_plumbing/tests/test_tier_public_metric.py passes] > public [real=no | gate=competitive | max-age-days=45 | when=every required public row of the arm is present and no older than 45 days, and the arm's list price (input plus output per million tokens) is no higher than the held default's; a dearer arm is only proposed] > own [real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the hub has run the shared cases that tier_metrics.csv names as the threshold for each arm compared and the spend is approved]

name: Quality tier default
purpose: The quality tier's default is the arm with the most capability on long-horizon structural work, with cost and speed counting weakly.
record: Score = C^0.85 x K^0.10 x S^0.05, weights fixed in tier_metrics.csv before any ranking. C = 0.20 x FrontierCode 2.0 + 0.15 x Terminal-Bench 4.0 + 0.15 x AA-Briefcase (Elo as a chance of beating the best arm) + 0.15 x HLE-Diamond + 0.10 x CritPt v2 + 0.10 x Terminal-Bench-Science + 0.10 x AA-Omniscience accuracy + 0.05 x AutomationBench-AA, each divided by the best eligible value. Floor: C at least 0.80. No imputation; rows older than 45 days are not used.
disadvantages: Same cost and time caveat; the evaluations are mostly one aggregator's runs; hard-subset evaluations have few tasks, so close arms are not separated. Cost per task is a proxy for the cost of the tier's typical call. The two validity rules of 2026-11-10 (added after the first ranking was seen: fit of evidence, and effort must be real) apply as for the balanced tier. The floor is relative to the best eligible arm, so a stronger top model raises the bar for the mid models; the owner may prefer a floor against a fixed reference.

name: Best tier default
purpose: The best tier's default is the arm with the highest independent capability score; cost and speed are not factors.
record: Score = the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0.1, nine evaluations in its published weights) of the arm. Cost and time never enter; on an exact tie the cheaper arm is shown first. No imputation; rows older than 45 days are not used.
disadvantages: A single composite from one aggregator; the index publishes no interval, so close arms at the top are not separated. The effort-must-be-real rule of 2026-11-10 (added after the first ranking was seen) applies: only each model's documented default effort competes until a caller applies a chosen effort.
cascading_conditionals: idea [kind=idea | scale=esoi/idea-rating-scale.md | min-pass-rate=0.75 | when=a new alternative is described: rate its description on the five questions of the scale before it is built] > offline [real=no | gate=all-pass | when=hubofhubs/the_world/model_plumbing/tests/test_tier_public_metric.py passes] > public [real=no | gate=competitive | max-age-days=45 | when=the arm's index row is present and no older than 45 days] > own [real=yes | gate=competitive | max-age-days=90 | when=the hub has run the shared cases that tier_metrics.csv names as the threshold for each arm compared and the spend is approved]
